policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: ASV 24:1 renders the verb only as 'Neither desire to be with them'. The qere תתאיו and the ketiv תתאו are the same verb with the same person, number and object; the difference is orthographic and leaves no trace in English, and the verse carries no ASV note mapped to this unit. Underdetermined; the qere base fallback carries the projection.

ASV 24:17 reads 'when thine enemy falleth' with the resumptive singular 'when he is overthrown'. That singular noun and pronoun render the qere אויבך (singular with 2ms suffix); the ketiv אויביך is the plural 'thine enemies', which the ASV would have rendered with a plural subject and 'they'. The English wording distinguishes the qere.
